Subject: Pricing: Confirming budget owner & $/1M token target

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. Quick recap and the asks I promised: we covered your expected monthly token volume (~300M–600M tokens/month depending on growth scenario), key latency SLAs (95th perc < 400ms), and your preference for a predictable committed pricing model vs purely usage-based.

To move an offer over to procurement/finance, can you confirm:
- Who is the economic buyer / budget owner for LLM infrastructure (name + email)?
- Does finance require a line-item estimate for $/1M tokens and an annual committed spend range? If so, please confirm target $/1M tokens you are aiming for (you mentioned a target in the $800–$1,200 range during the call).
- Any PO or legal procurement steps we should model (DocuSign, PO number cadence, SOW requirement)?

Next steps from our side: I’ll share an initial estimate for 1M token unit economics and two committed tiers (conservative & aggressive). Vivek will attach a short unit-econ workbook to illustrate cost vs throughput.

Attached: Redwood-pricing-estimate-1Mtokens.pdf (draft)

If you can loop in the person who signs off on budget, we’ll prepare an updated quote for procurement/finance. Would you like an intro call with Samir (our Solutions Engineering lead) or should we go straight to a finance email with the estimate?

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Appreciate the follow-up and the clear recap. A few answers:
- Economic buyer / budget owner is Samir Patel (Head of AI), samir@finexcorp.com — he owns the platform budget.
- Finance lead who handles procurement is Priya Rao (cc’d). She’ll need a line-item estimate and a simple one-page cost justification for the qtr/annual budget.
- We typically do a PO + SOW. DocuSign for signature is fine; procurement will request our standard vendor form.

For target unit economics: the leadership team has trajected target of around $1,000 per 1M tokens (we gave a range of $800–$1,200). We’re trying to keep below $1k ideally.

I’ll loop Samir and procurement once you drop the updated numbers. We’d like to see a committed option at ~300M tokens/month and a high-growth scenario at ~600M.

—Alex
Head of ML Platform | Finex Corp

Subject: Re: Pricing: Confirming budget owner & $/1M token target

Thanks Alex — quick note from SE perspective. I attached a very small unit economics workbook that maps:
- list price / token (hosted)
- committed discounts for 3-tier commit (150M / 300M / 600M)
- impact of KV cache and prefix caching on effective tokens billed (we model 10–25% savings for typical retrieval-heavy workloads)

Concretely, for your target of ~$1,000 per 1M tokens, a 300M/mo commit gets you to ~ $850–$950 per 1M depending on cache hit rates and batching config. At 600M/mo we can push to ~$720–$850 per 1M with deeper commitment + small quantization/throughput tuning.

I can run a quick sensitivity if you share a representative week of logs (token distribution by endpoint + latencies).

Attachment: redwood_unit_econ_v1.xlsx

—Vivek
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
